**Title:** DisPeD: A Controlled Study of Encoder Adaptation for Multi-Turn Jailbreak Detection

**Abstract:** Multi-turn jailbreak attacks spread adversarial intent across benign-seeming turns. Existing defenses fail to generalize: Llama Guard 3 detects only 1.8% of multi-turn jailbreaks zero-shot in our evaluation. Detecting such attacks benefits substantially from domain adaptation at base model scale, but the form of adaptation matters. We isolate the factors behind cross-attack generalization through controlled ablation: thirteen encoder configurations at base scale (125M–184M parameters) on synthetic multi-turn data decompose contributions of domain exposure, classification supervision, and label granularity across three out-of-distribution (OOD) attack families. On synthetic data, classification-based adaptation recovers OOD detection (F1 = 0.97–1.0 vs. vanilla 0.26–0.31; attack-side OOD, IID benign upper bound) while unsupervised pretraining collapses; under mixed-LLM training, template attacks remain detectable but strategy-diverse attacks degrade to chance level (F1 = 0.504). On human-authored single-turn data (ToxicChat), this hierarchy reverses: masked language modeling outperforms 9-class classification (F1 0.837 vs. 0.596). Classification adaptation's advantage is thus condition-specific rather than universal. Orthogonal to attack-side generalization, few-shot benign adaptation reduces false-positive rates from 58–68% to 0–1.5%, with 24.3× inference speedup (43× fewer parameters) over LLM-as-judge baselines.
